1.point: Sleep is set beside death; the dead have not gone far away, and this chapter will show, through the soul's worlds, its movement and the form its deeds give it, that what the soul becomes is in our hands.
steps: Open with the prayer that sets sleep beside the meeting with God
Move from sleep to death and to the common picture of barzakh as a distant waiting room
Overturn that picture with the lecturer's claim and state the chapter's three steps and conclusion

2.point: Creation has three depths (matter, images, intellects) that are dimensions of one world, so the dead in barzakh have gone deeper, not away.
steps: The soul is a copy of creation, so its three ways of knowing sample three worlds
Senses sample the material world; the other two are unseen but not far
Imagination samples a world of images that has shape without matter and exists in its own right
Intellect samples a world of pure meaning, the world of intellects
The world of images sits between the other two and is therefore called barzakh
The worlds are dimensions of this one world, differing in depth not distance
So the dead in barzakh are deeper in the world we live in, not elsewhere

3.point: The soul reaches the world of images whenever its hold on the body loosens (sleep, death, watchfulness), and unlike an angel how far it goes is decided by the life it lives.
steps: The soul stands between spirit and clay, so it has a share in each world
The body holds the soul's attention; the hold loosens at three times
Sleep: the soul touches the world of images (true dreams)
Death: the soul goes on in the image body, a matter of degree from sleep
Watchfulness: the attention is turned on purpose while awake
Angels have fixed stations and cannot move
The human soul has no fixed station; how far it goes depends on the life it lives

4.point: Our deeds now shape the image body we will meet after death.
steps: Repeated acts shape the self (habit)
The shaping shows faintly on the material body and far more on the image body
Authority: the next-world form is fixed by the soul's state at death
Qur'an and hadith: people appear in forms matching their natures; the faithful carry light
The reward is the deed itself made manifest, so the form is made of one's own deeds
Therefore the image body is being shaped now by what we do

5.point: The one self moves through three states, from commanding evil to peace, by acts we already know, so what it becomes is in our hands.
steps: If deeds shape the soul, the self is not fixed; the Qur'an names three states
The lowest state: the self commanding to evil, bound to the body by pleasure and worry
The second: the self that blames itself, a hopeful sign
The third: the self at peace
These are one self under different names, so a change of attitude changes the state
The means: remembrance, fasting and night prayer, which loosen the tie to the body
The soul takes on habits and is elastic, so what it becomes depends on what we do with it

¶1.label: advance
¶1.why: Supplies the hook: the prayer places sleep beside the meeting with God, the pairing the chapter builds on.

¶2.label: advance
¶2.why: Moves from sleep to death to barzakh and names the misconception (a distant waiting room) that the chapter corrects.

¶3.label: advance
¶3.why: Overturns the misconception with the lecturer's claim and states the chapter's thesis and three steps.

¶4.label: advance
¶4.why: Sets up the method the whole section uses: the soul as a copy of creation, three ways of knowing sampling three worlds.

¶5.label: advance
¶5.why: First world: senses meet matter; also establishes that 'unseen' means untrained, not distant, which ¶10 and ¶12 depend on.

¶6.label: support
¶6.why: Gives the example (mental picture, dream) that ¶7 uses to define the world of images; the step itself is drawn in ¶7.

¶7.label: advance
¶7.why: Second world: the world of images, defined from the sample and distinguished from private imagination.

¶8.label: advance
¶8.why: Third world: intellect grasps meaning without image or matter; the world of intellects.

¶9.label: advance
¶9.why: Places images between matter and intellect and names it barzakh, the link ¶12 needs to identify the dead's barzakh with this world.

¶10.label: advance
¶10.why: Supplies the key step: the worlds are dimensions of one world, deeper not farther.

¶11.label: restate
¶11.why: Summarises ¶5 to ¶10; adds no new step and ¶12 lands the conclusion anyway.

¶12.label: advance
¶12.why: Applies the dimensions picture to the graveside and lands the section's point.

¶13.label: advance
¶13.why: Shows why the soul has a share in each world: set between spirit and clay, with a counterpart in the world of images.

¶14.label: advance
¶14.why: States the governing idea of the section: the body's hold on attention, loosened at three times.

¶15.label: advance
¶15.why: First loosening, sleep, with the true dream as the sign that the soul has touched the world of images.

¶16.label: support
¶16.why: Lead-in to the Zumar verse that ¶17 draws on to make death a matter of degree from sleep; the step itself is taken in ¶17.

¶17.label: advance
¶17.why: Second loosening, death: sleep and death differ in degree, and introduces the image body.

¶18.label: advance
¶18.why: Reverses the picture of a body carrying the soul and establishes that the image body was there all along; Section 4 relies on this body.

¶19.label: advance
¶19.why: Third loosening, watchfulness: attention turned on purpose while awake, with Tabatabaʾi as witness.

¶20.label: restate
¶20.why: Summarises the three loosenings already given in ¶15, ¶17 and ¶19; no new step.

¶21.label: advance
¶21.why: The contrast case: angels have fixed stations and cannot move, which ¶22 needs.

¶22.label: advance
¶22.why: Lands the point: the human soul has no fixed station, and how far it goes is set by the life it lives.

¶23.label: advance
¶23.why: Raises the objection (nothing we do matters) and answers it with habit shaping the self, via the lying example.

¶24.label: advance
¶24.why: Moves from the material body, barely marked, to the image body, which sin deforms and piety lights; this is the section's core step.

¶25.label: advance
¶25.why: Supplies the authority that the next-world form is fixed by the soul's qualities at the moment of death.

¶26.label: support
¶26.why: Hadith lead-in and verse cue that back ¶25's claim about forms matching natures and set up the light that ¶27 uses.

¶27.label: advance
¶27.why: New step: the light is the believers' own deeds made manifest, so reward is the act itself.

¶28.label: restate
¶28.why: Its claim, that the image body is being shaped now by our deeds, was already made in ¶24; it adds only the Shomali tag line. The section lands twice.

¶29.label: restate
¶29.why: A recap of Sections 2 to 4 before the section begins; nothing in it is new or needed to start ¶30.

¶30.label: advance
¶30.why: Infers that the self is not fixed and names the first of the three states.

¶31.label: support
¶31.why: Glosses the Yusuf verse and adds worry as a second binding force, which ¶38 later picks up ('trained to worry about the body').

¶32.label: advance
¶32.why: Second state, the self that blames itself, read as a hopeful sign.

¶33.label: advance
¶33.why: Third state, the self at peace, reached by keeping up the self-blame.

¶34.label: advance
¶34.why: Supplies the decisive step: one self, three names by attitude, so the state can be changed.

¶35.label: advance
¶35.why: Begins the means of change with remembrance and cues the Raʿd verse.

¶36.label: support
¶36.why: Ties the verse's rest to the third state so the means in ¶35 connects to the goal in ¶33.

¶37.label: advance
¶37.why: Fasting and night prayer as further means, linked back to the loosening of the body's hold from Section 3.

¶38.label: advance
¶38.why: Explains why the means work (the soul takes on habits, is elastic) and lands the point that what it becomes depends on us.

¶39.label: restate
¶39.why: Chapter-wide summary; every sentence repeats a conclusion already landed in ¶12, ¶22, ¶28 or ¶38.

¶40.label: aside
¶40.why: A question the chapter does not answer, raised only as a bridge to the next; the point does not use it.
